high.title: Dollar jumps to R$ 5.06 and accumulates gains of over 3% with 'Flávio risk' and Middle East in focus
high.summary: The Brazilian Real weakened significantly as the USD/BRL pair closed at R$ 5.0678, up 1.63% on the day and reaching an intraday high of R$ 5.0818 - the strongest level in nearly a month. The Real accumulated a substantial 3.55% depreciation for the week, driven by increased risk aversion stemming from two key factors: geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and domestic political risk dubbed "Flávio risk." The latter relates to leaked audio involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro, creating political uncertainty ahead of presidential elections. The Dollar Index (DXY) also strengthened 0.47% to 99.292, indicating broader USD strength. Despite oil price gains that typically benefit Brazil as a commodity exporter, political risk overshadowed this positive factor. For FX traders, this represents a clear risk-off sentiment affecting emerging market currencies, with BRL particularly vulnerable to political noise. Watch for further developments in the political scandal and any central bank intervention signals.

high.title: Braskem (BRKM5) leads Ibovespa gains and CSAN3 worst performer; see weekly highlights
high.summary: The Ibovespa extended losses for a fifth consecutive week, falling 3.71% to close at 177,283.83 points amid Middle East conflicts and domestic political risk. The market focused on political noise during earnings season, particularly the leaked audio between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Banco Master's Daniel Vorcaro involving alleged US$ 24 million (approximately R$ 134 million) negotiations. This political uncertainty, combined with geopolitical tensions, created a risk-off environment that weighed heavily on Brazilian equities. The sustained five-week decline indicates persistent selling pressure and deteriorating investor sentiment toward Brazilian assets.

medium.title: With end of 'little blouse tax', Shopee and a FII segment have much to celebrate; see 3 recommendations to invest in this scenario
medium.summary: The elimination of the 20% import tax on international purchases up to US$ 50 was confirmed in the Official Gazette, potentially boosting e-commerce in Brazil. Companies like Mercado Livre, Amazon, and especially Shopee are expected to benefit from increased order flows and price competitiveness. The analyst highlights logistics real estate investment funds (FIIs) as beneficiaries, as Shopee holds significant warehouse space in Brazil. This policy change could drive increased demand for logistics infrastructure and benefit related REITs.
